newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse rocks then recovers, future unsure.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse rocks then recovers, future unsure.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ended a depressed but busy Friday with minor gains as benign U.S. producer price data and a rising Dow Jones lifted earlier gloom, but traders said the future remained uncertain.

"Let us see what Monday brings," one trader said. "The early decline today brought out the bottom fishers who thought it had gone too far, but it was the U.S. figures, New York and some end of week reaction that finally lifted the index."
The U.S. February Producer Price Index was down 0.4 percent, the biggest drop since October 1994. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which fell 160 points overnight, rose 70 at the open.
Star of the day on the Brussels bourse was insurer Royale Belge which rose 4.2 percent or 360 francs to close at 8,990 after at one stage hitting a new year high of 9,050 francs.

Traders said the announcement late on Thursday of profits of 11.3 billion francs in 1996, coupled with a declaration that the share value should be nearer 10,000 francs had lit the fuse on the shares.
Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere, which said on Thursday it had made a small profit of 391 million francs in 1996, rose 1.9 percent to 2,700 francs.
Banks BBL, Generale Bank and Kredietbank all lost some ground as speculation over a big Belgian bank merger in the near future faded.
BBL ended 20 francs down at 8,320, Generale Bank 75 francs lower at 13,450 and Kredietbank 50 easier at 13,200 francs.
The Bel-20 share index closed 1.06 points or 0.05 percent up at 2,192.88 after earlier diving 1.6 percent to 2,155.06.
A total of some four million francs of Belgian shares chenged hands.
